cases.protectedBehaviour: Find teaching that moves beyond the stated curriculum objective.
cases.materialDifference: A substantial teaching block introduces later curriculum content.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject an accurate example that stays inside the objective.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Keep related later notation or technique out when it competes with the current year objective.
cases.materialDifference: A lesson adds a substantial new formal convention from later progression on top of the new concept being taught.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject formalism required by the approved objective, supplied sequence or current year curriculum.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Permit formal notation or technique when it is part of the approved current objective and receives enough teaching and practice.
cases.materialDifference: The formal convention is the lesson's stated learning rather than an attached extension.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not remove required current learning merely because a younger year would use an informal representation.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find demand that is materially unsuitable for the year group.
cases.materialDifference: Required reading or reasoning assumes knowledge well beyond the stated year.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not remove necessary subject vocabulary that is taught and supported.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Keep the displayed objective semantically equal to the full objective.
cases.materialDifference: The child-facing shortening changes the intended learning.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not require identical wording when the shortening keeps the meaning.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept a different but sound lesson choice.
cases.materialDifference: The activity differs from the reviewer's likely preference but teaches the same objective well.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not report personal taste as a defect.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Correct a bounded contradiction between wording and values.
cases.materialDifference: The question asks how much more one character has when the other has more.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not redesign the lesson architecture for a local number correction.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find premature independence in genuinely new or difficult learning.
cases.materialDifference: Pupils move from one model to independent work without needed guided practice.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not assume every lesson needs the same amount of guided practice.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Permit omission of guided practice when the learning is already secure enough.
cases.materialDifference: The brief and lesson evidence establish secure prior learning before fresh independent use.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject the route only because Our Turn is absent.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find independent work that repeats the model's exact decision route.
cases.materialDifference: Surface details change but the answer path and decision are already completed in modelling.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject fresh procedural values when executing the procedure is the target.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept new values as fresh practice when executing the procedure is the learning.
cases.materialDifference: The method stays stable while pupils independently calculate new values.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not demand a different task architecture merely for variety.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find a worksheet that reuses the board's load-bearing decisions.
cases.materialDifference: The worksheet repeats the same evidence, classifications or conclusions as the lesson model.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject a familiar representation carrying genuinely unseen work.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find support that gives away the decision pupils must make.
cases.materialDifference: The stem names which character is wrong before pupils decide.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject a neutral stem that only helps pupils start expressing a reason.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find a dialogic route that does not permit several defensible positions.
cases.materialDifference: The discussion is framed around reaching one preselected correct view.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not treat correction of harmful or false claims as forced consensus.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find discovery work whose phenomenon is unsafe, unreliable or unrevealing.
cases.materialDifference: The exploration cannot dependably make the target pattern visible.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject a bounded exploration followed by explicit teaching.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find a Task-Centred route without one genuine sustained task.
cases.materialDifference: The route is a list of ordinary practice questions labelled as a real task.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject a sustained task that legitimately uses short enabling input.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Correct an existing picture brief that contradicts the settled lesson state.
cases.materialDifference: The lesson needs a plugged-in appliance but the brief requires it to be unplugged.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not change photo identity, source profile or authenticity class.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Return a new visual purpose to Lesson Designer.
cases.materialDifference: The honest repair requires a new photograph or a different authenticity boundary.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not create or remove photo objects during review.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Do not replace an unverified changing fact with another remembered figure.
cases.materialDifference: A load-bearing current statistic has no verified source.
cases.expectedResult: APPROVED WITH TEACHER FLAG OR STABLE BOUNDED CORRECTION
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not flag stable well-established subject facts merely because they are factual.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Leave physical presentation to downstream designers and visual review.
cases.materialDifference: The only concern is colour, type, spacing or page regions.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not report presentation taste as a lesson-design defect.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Trust deterministic validation to block malformed designs before semantic review.
cases.materialDifference: A required identifier or field is malformed.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not spend semantic review attention rechecking the malformed field.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Flag a choice only when teacher context can decide between sound options.
cases.materialDifference: Both difficulty choices are pedagogically sound and the brief does not settle the class need.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not label either sound option as defective.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find recorded work that hides the subject learning.
cases.materialDifference: The final record preserves activity but omits the evidence, method or justification taught.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not require a specific book layout when the selected medium shows the learning.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Keep support that enables the intended performance without supplying it.
cases.materialDifference: A reference tool reduces access load while pupils still make the target decision.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not remove support merely because the work is independent.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find support that performs the new thinking for pupils.
cases.materialDifference: The scaffold contains the classification, inference or answer pupils must generate.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject support that only reduces reading or recording load.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find a likely misconception that blocks the intended method or concept.
cases.materialDifference: The lesson depends on a distinction but never addresses the predictable wrong belief.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not demand a catalogue of every possible minor error.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find a sequence of individually plausible activities that never resolves and retests the lesson's central difficulty.
cases.materialDifference: The practical, explanation and questions touch the topic but do not build evidence around one blocking misconception or central gap.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not require one misconception when the lesson has no genuine misconception and a clear central difficulty already organises the sequence.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find a checking question whose answer is visible without using the target relationship or method.
cases.materialDifference: Children can choose correctly from an obvious picture or wording cue while still holding the misconception the lesson claims to assess.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject a deliberately brief recall check when recall is the stated evidence claim.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Keep success criteria usable for the performance children are learning.
cases.materialDifference: The criteria mix topic facts into a numbered procedure, so children cannot use them to complete or judge the target work.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject a labelled recognition reference merely because it is not a numbered procedure.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Require a short usable safety precaution before equipment is handled.
cases.materialDifference: The lesson asks children to handle equipment but gives neither an equipment-specific on-screen precaution nor teacher guidance.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not demand a separate safety lesson when one concise precaution controls the risk.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Protect the structure, scale, response form and demand of named test preparation.
cases.materialDifference: A multi-part grid task is reduced to separate easier checks.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not require the real protected item or its exact values to appear.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Correct one stale record line when the lesson and brief clearly agree.
cases.materialDifference: The lesson preserves the sound decision but the compact record names an earlier option.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not redesign a sound lesson to match a stale record.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Find purposeful drift from a sound recorded decision.
cases.materialDifference: The finished lesson quietly replaces the selected representation or learning demand.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not treat the decision record as higher authority than the teacher brief.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Reconsider the learning when correcting or replacing evidence removes a planned comparison.
cases.materialDifference: Year 4 objective: identify continuity and change in children's lives using a range of sources. The designer planned play and learning. A supposed toy in a portrait proves unsuitable evidence of play and becomes a comparison of painted and photographed portraits. The other two sources concern schooling. The final task permits any two sources and accepts an entirely schooling-based answer. The decision record calls this full coverage because the lesson also showed the portrait.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not restore the inaccurate toy inference, demand a fixed number of childhood topics, or change the objective to match the narrower task.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Judge replacements by the geographical learning they still enable, not by their being valid photographs.
cases.materialDifference: A geography lesson compares how people use two river locations. An unavailable photograph showing boats and a quay is replaced by an accurate close-up of water at that location. The comparison still asks how people use both locations, and the replacement shows no such use. The other source shows farming. Neither text nor another representation supplies the lost evidence.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject a different photograph or accessible text that actually preserves the required evidence merely because the original file changed.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept appropriate depth within an explicitly school-specific objective.
cases.materialDifference: The approved objective is to identify continuity and change in children's schooling using sources. A classroom photograph and a timetable supply different evidence, and the final answer compares school activities and equipment with today. Children use both sources meaningfully.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not demand work, play or home life to satisfy a different, broader objective.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept an accurate replacement that preserves the intended learning.
cases.materialDifference: A lesson comparing travel before and after motor transport replaces one unusable photograph of a horse-drawn bus with another verified photograph showing the same relevant transport features. Questions, comparisons and end performance remain supported; attribution is updated.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not demand a new lesson architecture solely because the source file or attribution changed.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept sources whose distinct contributions meet in the final comparison without a dependency between every adjacent source.
cases.materialDifference: Children examine evidence of past work and play, with time and place made clear. Both contributions are taught and used in a final comparison of childhood. Reversing the two source pairs changes no necessary prerequisite, but removing either loses a substantive part of the comparison.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject the sequence for lacking chronological order or invent a causal link between work and play.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Distinguish a new format from a new application decision.
cases.materialDifference: Teaching states that pupils still read and write while tools changed. Children select a paraphrase of that conclusion, then write it with evidence. An extra Apply asks whether everything about learning changed and accepts the same conclusion using the same evidence. Its rationale claims increased demand solely because it is now a claim to judge.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not ban immediate comprehension checks or repeated practice that serves learning; reconsider the unearned extra Apply.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept application when familiar knowledge must be used to decide a fresh case.
cases.materialDifference: After learning that changes to tools do not necessarily change an activity, children meet a new, accessible source showing both a changed tool and a changed activity. They must decide which earlier comparison still holds and which does not. Repeating the earlier conclusion unchanged gives an incorrect answer.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not reject this merely because it also uses a claim question or revisits continuity and change.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Retain enabling criteria and readable evidence during independent comparison.
cases.materialDifference: The task uses fresh sources. A visible feature table reminds children to compare matching aspects, identify continuity and change, and use details from both sources. It supplies no comparison or conclusion for those sources. Children can use or ignore it.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not remove the reference because the work is independent or require procedural numbered steps instead.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Require the knowledge needed for the intended explanation, not just a concrete topic example.
cases.materialDifference: The objective is to explain how an animal's features help it survive. Teaching shows a clear polar bear photograph and says it is suited to cold places, but gives no explanation of what its features do. Independent work asks children to explain how its fur helps it survive. Neither prior knowledge nor another source supplies the missing relationship.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not demand more animals, a story or a longer lesson when teaching the relevant relationship through this example is sufficient.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept a small concrete example that adequately prepares the target performance.
cases.materialDifference: Children observe and compare a toy car travelling down the same ramp onto two surfaces. The teacher explains how greater friction slows the car, referring to the observed motion. Children use a fresh comparable result to explain the difference. The representation and necessary reading support remain available.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not add technical vocabulary, a second phenomenon or extra facts merely to make the teaching richer.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept fresh values and purposeful repetition when executing the taught method is the learning.
cases.materialDifference: After modelled and guided reading of four-digit counter charts with empty columns, children read fresh charts. Zero moves between columns, all case types have been prepared, and the column-value reference remains visible. Children must read each chart to find its numeral; the set has no final trick question.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not replace fluency with puzzles, remove the reference or demand a written justification after every chart.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept the same conclusion when a fresh case requires independent examination of different evidence.
cases.materialDifference: Children learn to infer a character's feelings from actions and speech. In a fresh accessible passage, a different character is also anxious, but the clues are different. The question asks children to infer the feeling and explain which details support it. Repeating the earlier answer's evidence would be wrong.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not require a different emotion just to make the answer different, or ban reuse of the taught inference method.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Judge a fresh situation by the choice it leaves children, not its new names.
cases.materialDifference: Teaching models listening without interrupting through a disagreement. A worksheet labelled fresh application changes only the children's names and asks which is better: listening or interrupting. The preceding slide has given that exact choice and conclusion. No new circumstance, action to formulate or evidence to interpret changes the work.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not ban an immediate recall check, a familiar reminder, or rehearsal of the listening behaviour when that is the declared purpose.

cases.protectedBehaviour: Match picture evidence requirements to the explanation and pupil decision.
cases.materialDifference: A geography task asks children to explain how a bridge connects homes to a school across a river. The picture request requires only a river with buildings and permits images showing no crossing or school. The designer has supplied no map or text carrying those relationships, yet the model answer assumes they are visible.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not require one exact photograph, architecture style or camera angle when several truthful representations could show the needed relationships.

cases.materialDifference: A worksheet provides written accounts of learning and play, but references a board criterion requiring a detail from the toys and a detail from the written account. No toys appear in the worksheet. Its intended comparison and required evidence are otherwise explicit.
cases.protectedBehaviour: Check resolved support against the task that uses it.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not add toys or change the task merely to satisfy the stale criterion, or remove needed support. Correct its source wording for this use.

cases.materialDifference: A maths sheet has no printed chart. Its design explicitly retains the blank place-value chart and criteria on the board while children complete the sheet in class. The chart is suitable and does not reveal the fresh answers.
cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept planned access without duplicating support on every sheet.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not require a printed chart solely because the worksheet reference list is empty.

cases.materialDifference: A sheet intended for use away from the classroom asks children to use the classification key from the board. The key is neither printed nor included in another available resource; its classifications cannot be inferred from the task alone.
cases.protectedBehaviour: Require usable support access when a task depends on it.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not invent access to the board or change the learning to unaided recall. Preserve the intended classification task while providing the needed resource.

cases.materialDifference: A fresh comparison uses different written sources but the retained criteria ask for a matching aspect, a continuity or change, and details from both sources. Each instruction fits the new work and none supplies its answer.
cases.protectedBehaviour: Reuse valid support rather than rewriting it for novelty.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not rewrite suitable criteria just because the sources changed.

cases.materialDifference: A source comparison explicitly establishes that reading continues while its materials differ. A brief claim question asks whether everything changed and children rehearse the supported comparison. It is labelled consolidation within practice; a later fresh task supplies independent evidence.
cases.protectedBehaviour: Accept a supported check when its limited purpose is honest.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not ban the claim question or require it to become harder when it serves consolidation.

cases.materialDifference: A source comparison explicitly establishes that reading continues while its materials differ. The same claim question asks whether everything changed, but is the sole final evidence of fresh independent comparison. The supplied conclusion answers it without children selecting or interpreting new evidence.
cases.protectedBehaviour: Distinguish the same supported question from evidence of fresh independent judgement.
cases.forbiddenFinding: Do not ban claim questions generally. The finding concerns what this task can establish about the intended learning.
